chunks: From him, from Abū Yaḥyā al-Wāsiṭī, from some of his companions, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “Should the person in janābah rinse his mouth?” He said: “No; only the exterior becomes junub.”

key_terms.إِنَّمَا: only; restricting the ruling to what follows
key_terms.الظَّاهِرُ: the exterior or outward part of the body
key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: a person in the state of janābah (major ritual impurity)

ai.seo_question: Does a person in janābah need to rinse the mouth because of major ritual impurity?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning janābah and ritual purity. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that janābah pertains to the outward body, indicating that rinsing the mouth is not required on that basis.
